This Agenda contains a brief general description of each item to be considered. Copies of the Staff reports or
 other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office
 of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. Any person who has a question concerning any of the
 agenda items may call the City Manager at (310) 603-0220, ext. 200.

  Procedures for Addressing the Council

 IN ORDER TO EXPEDITE CITY COUNCIL BUSINESS, WE ASK THAT ALL PERSONS WISHING TO
 ADDRESS  THE  COUNCIL  SUBMIT  YOUR  COMMENTS  IN  ADVANCE  TO
 CITYCLERK@LYNWOODCA.GOV OR FILL OUT A FORM PROVIDED AT THE PODIUM, AND TO TURN IT
 IN TO THE CITY CLERK PRIOR TO THE START OF THE MEETING. FAILURE TO FILL OUT SUCH A
 FORM WILL PROHIBIT YOU FROM ADDRESSING THE COUNCIL IN THE ABSENCE OF THE
 UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF THE COUNCIL.

  NON-AGENDA PUBLIC ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

 THIS PORTION PROVIDES AN OPPORTUNITY FOR THE PUBLIC TO ADDRESS THE
 COUNCIL ON ITEMS WITHIN THE JURISDICTION OF THE COUNCIL AND NOT LISTED
 ON THE AGENDA. IF AN ITEM IS NOT ON THE AGENDA, THERE SHOULD BE NO
 SUBSTANTIAL DISCUSSION OF THE ISSUE BY THE COUNCIL, BUT COUNCIL MAY
 REFER THE MATTER TO STAFF OR SCHEDULE SUBSTANTIVE DISCUSSION FOR A
 FUTURE MEETING. (The Ralph M. Brown Act, Government Code Section 54954.2 (a).)

 8. CONSENT CALENDAR
 ALL MATTERS LISTED UNDER THE CONSENT CALENDAR WILL BE ACTED UPON BY
 ONE MOTION AFFIRMING THE ACTION RECOMMENDED ON THE AGENDA. THERE
 WILL BE NO SEPARATE DISCUSSION ON THESE ITEMS PRIOR TO VOTING UNLESS
 MEMBERS OF THE COUNCIL OR STAFF REQUEST SPECIFIC ITEMS TO BE REMOVED
 FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR FOR SEPARATE ACTION.

 8.1 APPROVAL OF THE WARRANT REGISTER
  Comments:
  City of Lynwood warrant register dated April 1, 2025 for FY 2024-2025. (FIN)

  Recommendation:
  Staff respectfully recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood approve the
  warrant register dated April 1, 2025 for FY 2024-2025

 8.2 PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES
  Comments:
  The purpose of this item is to have the Lynwood City Council review and approve the
  March 18, 2025 City Council meeting action minutes. (CC)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the Lynwood City Council approve the March 18, 2025 Regular
  Meeting and Closed Session Regular Meeting Action Minutes.

City Council Regular Meeting
  2
  8.3 FIRST AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  CONSERVATION CORPS OF LONG BEACH
  Comments:

  Staff are requesting that the City Council approve First Amendment to the Professional
  Service Agreement with Conservation Corps of Long Beach to perform clean up services
  through June 30, 2025. (CM)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council a pprove a Resolution, First Amendment to the
  Public Service Agreement with Conservation Corps of Long Beach for the purpose of
  providing additional cleanup efforts throughout the City.

 8.4 A RESOLUTION APPROVING A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  JOE A. GONSALVES TO PROVIDE LEGISLATIVE SERVICES TO THE CITY
  Comments:
  As the City continues to navigate various legislative challenges, the expertise of Joe A.
  Gonsalves remains essential in navigating these issues. The Professional Services
  Agreement, which expired on June 30, 2024, provided specific legislative services to be
  performed by Joe A. Gonsalves, as needed by the City. Entering into a new agreement
  will ensure that Mr. Gonsalves can continue to focus on legislative advocacy and other
  key priorities on behalf of the City. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council approve a Professional Services Agreement with
  Joe A. Gonsalves for State Lobbying Services.

 9.  NEW/OLD BUSINESS

 9.1
  HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT - 2024

  Comments:
  Receive and File 2024 Annual Housing Progress Report update submitted to the State
  Office of Planning and Research and the Department of Housing and Community
  Development. (CD)

  Recommendation:
  Receive and File 2024 Annual Housing Progress Report update submitted to the State
  Office of Planning and Research and the Department of Housing and Community
  Development.

City Council Regular Meeting
  3
  9.2 SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 1785, AMENDING
  LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 7-17.1 - ESTABLISHMENT AND
  DESIGNATION OF TRUCK TRAFFIC ROUTES
  Comments:
  The City Council at its March 18, 2025 meeting introduced Ordinance No. 1785, which
  will update section 7-17.1 of the Lynwood Municipal Code by adding or removing street
  segments from the existing truck routes. This ordinance is now being presented for
  second reading and adoption. If adopted this evening, Ordinance No. 1785 will become
  effective 30 days from this date. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council conduct the second reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 1785 , “AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD,
  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AMENDING SECTION 7-17.1
  “ESTABLISHMENT AND DEISGNATION OF TRUCK TRAFFIC ROUTES” OF CHAPTER
  TITLE 7-17 “RESTRICTIONS ON USE OF STREETS BY OVERWEIGHT AND
  OVERSIZE VEHICLES” OF THE LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE”

 SUBJECT:  FIRST AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  WITH CONSERVATION CORPS OF LONG BEACH

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council a pprove a Resolution, First Amendment to the Public
 Service Agreement with Conservation Corps of Long Beach for the purpose of providing
 additional cleanup efforts throughout the City.

 Background:

 The Conservation Corps of Long Beach is a community youth development organization that
 continually seeks meaningful projects for young people to gain valuable experience while
 contributing to the enhancement of their community and environment. Established in 1987,
 CCLB is one of 14 State Certified Community Corps programs in California.

 To fulfill its mission, CCLB combines its state-accredited alternative high school program with
 hands-on conservation work projects. These projects include, but are not limited to, urban
 forestry, habitat restoration, recycling, graffiti removal, fire fuel reduction, invasive vegetation
 treatment, community garden development, and construction. Through these efforts, CCLB
 provides young people with marketable job skills while helping to preserve and restore the
 local environment.

 Discussion and Analysis:

City Council City Council Regular Meeting

  At its regular meeting of July 16, 2024, the Lynwood City Council approved Resolution No.
 2024.091 amending the revised adopted Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25 budget which in part
 appropriated $100,000 to implement a citywide cleanliness program.

 In response to the Council’s direction, a citywide cleanup strike force was established, and
 staff collaborated with the Conservation Corps of Long Beach (CCLB) to support the cleanup
 efforts. Under the authority of the City Manager, a Professional Services Agreement was
 executed on December 2, 2024, at a not-to-exceed amount of $50,000.

 Supervised by the Public Works Department, CCLB provides a five-member crew who work
 from approximately 7:15 a.m. to 2:15 p.m., four days a week, to service the City’s parks and
 major thoroughfares. The crew collects and disposes of trash in parks on Mondays and
 Fridays, while streets are serviced on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The CCLB team is
 responsible for cleaning Lynwood public rights-of-way (ROW) thoroughfares, including bulky
 item pickups, as well as weed and trash removal from tree wells, sidewalks, and parkways
 along the following streets:

  Abbott Road
  Imperial Highway
  Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard
  Alameda Street
  Santa Fe Avenue
  State Street
  Long Beach Boulevard
  Atlantic Boulevard

 The collaboration with CCLB has been positive and allows the Public Works division to attend
 to other skilled tasks and responsibilities. The cost of CCLB services is much lower in contrast
 to the costs incurred to perform the same tasks by city employees.

 Staff is requesting that City Council to continue CCLB services for citywide cleanup through
 June 30, 2025. Additionally, staff will recommend funding CCLB in the next Fiscal Budget of
 2025-26.

 Fiscal Impact:

 Cost for services is included in the current FY 2024/25 budget.

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council conduct the second reading and adopt Ordinance No.
 1785 , “AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY
 OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AMENDING SECTION 7-17.1
 “ESTABLISHMENT AND DEISGNATION OF TRUCK TRAFFIC ROUTES” OF CHAPTER
 TITLE 7-17 “RESTRICTIONS ON USE OF STREETS BY OVERWEIGHT AND OVERSIZE
 VEHICLES” OF THE LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE”

 Background:

 The City of Lynwood currently has designated truck routes. To ensure consistency among the
 Municipal Code, the General Plan, and to keep trucks on properly designed roadways, staff
 requested traffic engineering consultant Bowman Infrastructure Engineers (IE) to review and
 update the existing truck routes. IE has completed their review and provided an updated truck
 route report along with a proposed truck routes map. The report includes recommendations for
 street segments to be added or removed from the existing truck routes based on field
 investigations.
 California Vehicle Code Section 35701 authorizes the City to adopt ordinances prohibiting the
 use of streets by commercial vehicles that exceed designated gross weight limits, with certain
 exceptions. In 2010, the City of Lynwood adopted Ordinance No. 1629, which established
 designated truck routes under Lynwood Municipal Code Section 7-17.1. The California Air
 Resources Board (CARB), in its April 2005 “Air Quality and Land Use Handbook,” recognized
 that living near high-traffic areas can lead to adverse health effects, including respiratory
 issues and asthma exacerbations, especially in children. Similarly, the United States
 Environmental Protection Agency has noted that people living, working, or attending school
 near major roads experience a higher incidence of health problems, including asthma,

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  73
  cardiovascular disease, and reduced lung function, as well as increased exposure to road
 noise. To ensure consistency between the Municipal Code and the General Plan, staff
 requested Bowman Infrastructure Engineers to review the truck routes.

 On May 29, 2024, the City received the Truck Route report, which includes the Traffic
 Engineer’s findings and recommendations. The City Council recognizes the potential adverse
 effects of oversized trucks passing through residential neighborhoods and acknowledges the
 threats these pose to the health, safety, and welfare of the residents. The City Council finds
 that this amendment to the Municipal Code is necessary to preserve the public welfare, health,
 and safety of Lynwood residents.

 Discussion and Analysis:

 The report submitted on May 29, 2024 recommended removing Franklin Street from Los
 Flores Boulevard to Fernwood Avenue as a truck route, as this segment is located in a
 residential area. Bellinger Street is a more suitable alternative for commercial vehicles.

 The report also recommended designating Los Flores Boulevard from Santa Fe Avenue to
 Bellinger Street as a truck route. Although the south side is residential, this segment frequently
 accommodates oversized vehicles due to the businesses on the north side, making it a more
 practical route for commercial vehicles traveling southbound on Santa Fe Avenue.

 Additionally, the report also suggested designating Long Beach Boulevard from Imperial
 Highway to Louise Street as a truck route. This section is a major arterial road with
 commercial zoning, and the City developed the Northgate Market at the intersection of Long
 Beach Boulevard and Louise Street, which requires access for commercial vehicles.

 The report also suggested designating Louise Street from Long Beach Boulevard to Lewis
 Street and Lewis Street from Louise Street to its northern end.

 Finally, the report noted that there are currently no signs indicating truck route restrictions
 along the segment of Long Beach Boulevard between Imperial Highway and Louise Street,
 and IE recommended installing truck route signs for this section.

 In addition to these recommendations, staff received a request to restrict truck travel along
 Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard between Ernestine Street and Atlantic Avenue from 3 PM to
 9 AM. The Traffic Engineer reviewed this request and provided an updated Truck Route
 Report on October 2, 2024, which proposed extending the restriction to cover Martin Luther
 King Jr. Boulevard from Imperial Highway to Atlantic Avenue during the same hours. On
 August 26, 2024, the PSTP Commission approved the implementation of time restrictions on
 MLK Jr. Boulevard from Imperial Highway to Atlantic Avenue.

 Because the changes on the City’s current truck route necessitated an amendment to the
 ordinance, on February 27, 2025, staff took the item with the proposed ordinance amendment
 back to the PSTP Commission. The Commission reviewed the recommendations again and
 approved the item, however the commission requested that the City consider extending
 restrictions on Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard from Atlantic Avenue to Wright Road.

 Staff contacted the Traffic Engineer regarding this request accordingly. The Traffic Engineer

  responded that extending the restriction to Wright Road would leave trucks with no alternate
 route to reach Wright Road during restricted hours, other than using Imperial Highway. While
 Wright Road is a designated truck route, with the entire south side primarily used for
 manufacturing and truck traffic, it is important to note that nearly the entire north side of Wright
 Road is residential and could potentially cause concerns from residents. Additionally, Wright
 Road is narrower, with one lane in each direction and a right of way of approximately 60 feet.
 In contrast, Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard has two travel lanes in each direction and a wider
 right of way of about 100 feet. The Traffic Engineer stated that although it is up to the City,
 extending the restrictions to Wright Road is not advisable. Staff concurred with the Traffic
 Engineer's response and recommended the same to City Council.

 At the March 18th, 2025 City Council Meeting City Council approved the PSTP request to
 extend the restrictions on Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard from Atlantic Avenue to Wright

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City of Lynwood Housing Authority Board adopt the attached
 resolution entitled “A RESOLUTION OF THE LYNWOOD HOUSING AUTHORITY AS
 HOUSING SUCCESSOR TO THE LYNWOOD REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY AUTHORIZING
 THE ALLOCATION OF UNAPPROPRIATED LOW AND MODERATE INCOME HOUSING
 ASSET FUND (LMIHAF) IN THE AMOUNT OF $75,000 FOR DESIGNATED LEGAL
 SERVICES TO THE LYNWOOD HOUSING AUTHORITY PROVIDED BY KANE, BALLMER &
 BERKMAN, A PROFESSIONAL CORPORATION.”

 Background:

 In 2018, the Lynwood Housing Authority entered into an agreement with the law firm of Kane
 Ballmer & Berkman (“KBB”), a professional law corporation, to assist with the complicated
 issues involving a lawsuit (the “Rogel I Judgment”) and settlement as related to the
 construction of affordable housing units. KBB has provided ongoing legal representation in
 connection with the Rogel I Judgment including the negotiation, drafting, and implementation
 of a Disposition and Development Agreement (“DDA”) with Lynwood Family Apartments (the
 developer contracted to produce the affordable housing units) and the issuance of Housing
 Bond financing for the affordable housing units. The Lynwood Housing Authority needs to
 continue the services of KBB until the Lynwood Housing Authority has satisfied the Rogel I
 Judgment. However, it was recently discovered that the funding needed for KBB services was
 not included in the City's FY 2024-25 Annual Operating Budget. It is now being requested to
 approve the attached resolution that includes the needed budget adjustment to the City's FY

Lynwood Housing Authority Lynwood Housing Authority

  2024-25 Annual Operating Budget to cover expenditures as related to special legal counsel for
 the Lynwood Housing Authority as related to the Rogel I Judgment.

 Discussion and Analysis:

 KBB is a law firm with a long history of representation of public entities in matters involving the
 negotiation of disposition and development agreements for significant projects. KBB has
 represented the City of Lynwood and its constituent entities for more than two decades. The
 firm is intimately familiar with and has worked on many of the more significant projects in the
 City. KBB is currently providing designated legal services to the Lynwood Housing Authority
 as related to the Rogel I Judgment. A budget adjustment is needed to the City's FY 2024-25
 Annual Operating Budget in an amount not to exceed $75,000 to continue these services, as
 funds were inadvertently not included at the time the budget was completed.

 Fiscal Impact:

 There will be no fiscal impact to the General Fund. Funds for KBB services will come from the
 unappropriated fund balance of the Lynwood Housing Authority’s Low and Moderate Income
 Housing Asset Fund (LMIHAF).A budget adjustment is needed to reflect an appropriation for
 use of said unappropriated LMIHAF balance as follows:
